greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. With two days to go until Victoria votes, here's what's worth knowing.

lead.headline: Coalition would lease part of Melbourne's sewerage network to cut debt
lead.summary: Costings released by the Coalition include a 90-year lease of part of the network, as part of a plan it says would lower net debt by $20 billion over four years. Opposition Leader Jess Wilson rejects that this privatises Melbourne Water and says water bills will stay regulated and won't change because of the lease.

stories.headline: AI model designs working proteins from plain-language prompts
stories.summary: This Nature paper, first published in October and picked up in the press this month, presents Pinal, which turns text descriptions into candidate protein sequences. Lab tests found some designs worked, though many candidates did not.

stories.headline: Quantum simulator explores matter far from equilibrium with up to 180 qubits
stories.summary: A Nature paper from QuEra and Berkeley Lab, published in early November and announced on 18 November, used a neutral-atom machine to study long-lived 'prethermal' states and how they melt. It drew trade press coverage for the scale of the experiments.

stories.headline: AI agents take on the job of curating scientific training data
stories.summary: Published in Nature Communications on 4 November, this paper describes AIDE, a multi-agent system that automates data curation for scientific language models. The authors report its datasets can match or beat manually curated ones.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang still faces Congress despite return as Nvidia CEO
stories.summary: Lawmakers say Huang's reinstatement doesn't cancel the planned December hearings. The 1 December House interview also falls on the day Huang had been due to give Nvidia's GTC keynote in Washington.

stories.headline: OpenAI preprint claims to settle a famous maths-of-computing question
stories.summary: A preprint, not yet peer-reviewed, claims the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4. If it holds up it would be a major theory result, though it doesn't by itself give a practically faster method, so treat it as unverified for now.

stories.headline: Amazon buys Decart's AI chip software and hires its team
stories.summary: Amazon confirmed the deal for software meant to get more performance from its Trainium and Inferentia chips. It didn't disclose a price; Bloomberg reported about US$7.5 billion, and regulators still need to clear it.

stories.headline: Data centre anger becomes an election issue
stories.summary: An ABC analysis says concern about data centres has risen quickly among voters, with strong local opposition near sites such as one beside homes in West Footscray.

stories.headline: Teenager refused bail after fatal CBD stabbing
stories.summary: An 18-year-old charged with affray over a La Trobe Street brawl in which 21-year-old Rory Conroy was fatally stabbed has been remanded. A 17-year-old charged over the incident was also remanded.

stories.headline: Virgin strikes could disrupt flights, including from Melbourne
stories.summary: A union says workers will hold short stoppages at Melbourne and three other airports in a dispute over pay and shifts, which could cause delays. Virgin says it expects no effect on passengers.

stories.headline: Williamstown wrecking yard fire disrupts trains
stories.summary: Wednesday afternoon's blaze destroyed seven cars and damaged an office block, with no injuries reported. Buses replaced trains on the Altona Loop.

stories.headline: Blast in Sanaa as missiles are intercepted over Riyadh
stories.summary: An explosion hit Yemen's capital after recent air strikes near its airport. The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh.

stories.headline: Kim Jong Un calls for wider tactical nuclear deployment
stories.summary: North Korean state media says Kim also wants more nuclear material produced, and warned that denying the country's nuclear status would amount to a declaration of war.

thought: The best way to predict the future is to invent it. - Alan Kay
